text:
maria: Customer (acme-sre) escalated — their app intermittently fails to reach our private service endpoint in their VPC. They see resolution flip between the right private IP and NXDOMAIN.

acme-sre: We started seeing 5xxs from our side around 08:12 UTC. Pod logs show TLS handshake failures to private-endpoint.redwood.internal and lots of DNS failures. Happens across AZs, not just one node.

maria: Can you paste a failing dig +short and /etc/resolv.conf from a problematic node? Also any custom DNS forwarders in the VPC?

acme-sre: Here are extracts:
```
$ dig +short private-endpoint.redwood.internal @10.0.0.2
# sometimes returns 10.100.5.12 then empty line (no answer)
$ dig private-endpoint.redwood.internal @10.0.0.2 +short; echo $?
(nothing)
$ cat /etc/resolv.conf
nameserver 172.31.0.2
search ip-172-31-ec2.internal
options single-request
```

acme-sre: We have a forwarder EC2 (10.0.10.5) that we added last month for filtering. Resolver rule forwards *.internal to 10.0.10.5.

kevin: Noted. Two likely suspects: (1) the forwarder EC2 sometimes fails and returns NXDOMAIN/empty answers; (2) split-horizon: Route53 private hosted zone not associated with the VPC that is hitting the forwarder, so forwarder has no mapping for the private zone.

sam: Can you run these quick checks and paste results?
- aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name "redwood.internal"
- aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id Z12345... (for the private zone) and verify VPCs associated
- iptables -L on the forwarder, and systemd-resolve status

acme-sre: Ran list-hosted-zones-by-name, output shows the private zone is in our infra account but associated only with VPCs in acct-A. The VPC where pods run (acct-B) is not associated. We have a resolver rule in acct-B that forwards to the forwarder in acct-B.

jess: That matches a classic split-horizon/forwarder gap: queries from pods go to the forwarder (because of the resolver rule), the forwarder doesn't forward into Route53's VPC resolver for the private zone, so it returns NXDOMAIN. When it occasionally falls back to the VPC resolver (e.g., due to cache or route change) you see the correct private IP.

kevin: Two remediation paths: (A) associate the Route53 private hosted zone with the VPC in acct-B (preferred); (B) change the outbound resolver rule so queries for redwood.internal go to the AmazonProvidedDNS (VPC resolver) instead of the EC2 forwarder; (C) make the forwarder forward queries to the VPC resolver (10.0.0.2) so it can answer private hosted zones.

maria: Customer asked for a short-term workaround that doesn't require hosted zone permissions. Any ideas?

sam: Quick workaround: update the resolver rule priority to prefer AmazonProvidedDNS for the redwood.internal pattern or add an exception so the forwarding rule excludes redwood.internal. Another option is adding an /etc/hosts entry on the app nodes, but that's brittle.

acme-sre: We tried adding an exception on the forwarder but couldn't find where to add it in our distro's dnsmasq config. We can associate the hosted zone but need an IAM ticket.

maria: I'll create an ops ticket to request hosted zone association from infra and CC acme-sre. Meanwhile, sam — can you draft a short how-to for customers using forwarders, so support can advise them? Include commands and a minimal troubleshooting checklist.

sam: Draft checklist:
1) Confirm which resolver is answering: run `dig +short @169.254.169.253 whoami.local` (or your VPC resolver IP) and `dig +short @<forwarder-ip> private-endpoint.redwood.internal`.
2) Check Route53 private hosted zone associations: `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id <zone-id>` -> look at VPCs[].
3) If using a forwarding resolver, ensure it forwards unknown queries to the VPC resolver (10.0.0.2) or to the AWS Route53 Resolver inbound endpoint. Example dnsmasq forwarder config: `server=/redwood.internal/10.0.0.2`
4) Check forwarder health and caches (restart dnsmasq/unbound).
5) As temporary band-aid, add hosts entry or use a CNAME to a public resolvable name (not ideal).

jess: Also call out TLS symptom: if the forwarder returns a public IP (or wrong svc IP) the client will hit an endpoint with the wrong cert and fail TLS handshake — that's why they saw TLS errors earlier.

maria: Good. I'll share that with the customer and open the hosted zone association request. acme-sre, please confirm when you can grant assoc perms or we can accept a ticket.

acme-sre: Granting perms now, will update once association is done. Thanks for the quick triage. :raised_hands:

deploy-bot: Note — we observed a small spike in 502s to private endpoints at 08:12 UTC from data plane metrics (spike lasted ~3m). No infra deploys around that time.

maria: Closing loop once hosted zone assoc is confirmed and customer verifies resolution stable.
